title: A draggable readout pill shows it can be grabbed when the pointer is over it
goal: An arrow caption pill and a caliper number can both be dragged, but nothing tells you so until you try. When the pointer rests on a pill that can be moved, the app should give a small cue, such as the open-hand cursor or a faint lift, so a first-time user finds the drag without being told.
notes: Both grabs live in CanvasView.mouseDown: captionPillRect(_:) for arrows (captionDrag) and measureReadoutRect(_:) for calipers (measureHandleDrag .head). Cursor rects or a mouseMoved check against those rects with NSCursor.openHand / closedHand is the smallest version. Filed from the caption-drag audit rough item 1 and the caliper-head audit rough item 1.
acceptance: Hovering a selected arrow caption pill or a selected caliper number changes the cursor to the grab hand (and a closed hand while dragging).
No cue appears on an unselected arrow or caliper, where a press moves the whole object.
The cue does not appear over the endpoint handles, which keep their own behaviour.
Verified on the probe app; audit rough lines in queue/audits/2026-09-02-caption-drag.json and 2026-09-02-caliper-head.json updated or referenced.
